  <section v="14">

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The reason that even the arousal of natural emotions is specifically through the intellect is explained by the root of man being in Tikkun, where the primary element is the intellect and emotions follow it.

translations.translation: And the reason for this
(that even the arousal of natural emotions is specifically through the intellect)
is,
that the root of man is in Tikkun
[for the root of animals is in Tohu and the root of man is in Tikkun],
and in the world of Tikkun the primary element is the intellect,
and even the emotions of Tikkun are according to the intellect.
For although even in Tikkun the root of the emotions is above the root of the intellect,
for Abba and Imma are included in Mazla and Zeir Anpin is attached and dependent on Atika,
nevertheless,
their drawing down is through the intellect.
For among the distinctions between the emotions of Tohu and the emotions of Tikkun is,
that in Tohu the emotions were revealed as they are from their root in Keter
[and this is one of the explanations that the Sefiros of Tohu were in the aspect of crowns],
and the emotions of Tikkun are according to the intellect.
And from this it also descends to man, whose root is in Tikkun,
that his emotions
(even the natural emotions)
are according to the intellect.
And the difference between natural emotions and intellectual emotions is,
that in intellectual emotions
(although their root is in the essence of the soul above the intellect)
it is primarily felt that they are emotions of a man
(emotions of Tikkun)
whose primary element is intellect,
and in natural emotions
(although their arousal is through the intellect)
it is primarily felt that their root is in the essence of the soul which is above intellect.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: In the two expressions "Lech" and "Kol," the two types of emotions—natural and intellectual—are alluded to, with natural emotions relating to the root in Keter (Lech) and intellectual emotions relating to being drawn from the intellect (Kol).

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that in the two expressions "Lech" and "Kol" are also alluded the two types of emotions
(natural emotions and intellectual emotions).
And the explanation is,
that this which was explained above, that the emotions as they are in their root are in a state of nullification,
"Lech,"
the intention is
(primarily)
to this, that the root of the emotions is in Keter
(and correspondingly in man,
this is that the root of the emotions is in the essence of the soul),
for since Keter is separate from all the Sefiros,
therefore,
when the Sefiros
(the emotions and the intellect)
are included in Keter,
they are in a state of absence of existence.
However, regarding this that the emotions are drawn from the intellect,
since the intellect is a cause for the emotions,
therefore even when the emotions are included in the intellect,
they are in an aspect of existence.
And based on this it can be said,
that natural emotions,
in which it is felt that their root is in the essence of the soul,
belong to "Lech,"
and intellectual emotions belong to "Kol."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The connection to "and he found a hundred gates" for Yitzchak's sowing is that through sowing the emotions of the Nefesh HaElokis into the Nefesh HaBahamis, both the measured emotions of Tikkun and the unbounded emotions of Tohu are drawn, and this finding is beyond the measure of service.

translations.translation: And this is the connection and relevance of "and he found a hundred gates" to "and Yitzchak sowed,"
the sowing of the powers of the Nefesh HaElokis into the Nefesh HaBahamis
(and correspondingly in the performance of the mitzvos),
for the emotions of the Nefesh HaElokis, whose root is in Tikkun, are in measure and limitation according to the intellect,
and the emotions of the Nefesh HaBahamis, whose root is in Tohu, are in unbounded intensity,
and through the sowing of the emotions of the Nefesh HaElokis into the emotions of the Nefesh HaBahamis, a hundred gates are drawn,
twice fifty,
emotions of Tikkun and emotions of Tohu.
And it can be said,
that what is written "and he found a hundred gates,"
that "finding" is not according to the measure of service,
is,
for the emotions of the soul are beyond comparison relative to their root,
the emotions of Tikkun,
and all the more so the emotions of the Nefesh HaBahamis
(whose emotions are in the lusts of this world)
are beyond comparison relative to their root in the emotions of Tohu.
And therefore,
the drawing down of the hundred gates,
emotions of Tikkun and emotions of Tohu,
through the emotions of the Nefesh HaElokis refining the emotions of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
is a finding that is not according to the measure of service.
